notes.text: There are horizontal strips of unblurred regions of the exterior map, which extend infinitely out from roughly the corners of the map. The side towards the map center is a hard line, while the outer side appears to be feathered; see `dev/Unblurred Exterior Map Strips.jpg` for a visual illustration

Especially at high zoom levels, the district labels cluster together and become illegible. District labels should disappear when the zoom level falls below 12. Also, lets try styling them using the Impact font (available in `public/assets/fonts/`), slightly reduced opacity, and a darker grey color to make them a bit less obtrusive while still being visible.

(Related to Pin 4) Many of the white-listed street labels are repeated far too many times, often to the point of overlapping each other (see `dev/Excessive & Overlapping Street Labels.jpg`).  At the same time, in other cases, street labels aren't appearing at all for the visible segment of a street.  I'm not sure if we're coming up against the limits of the control we can have over these labels; let me know if a balance needs to be decided upon, but otherwise if this can be improved, pelase do.

Please see `dev/Orientation Street White List v2.md` for a revised csv code block for the white list itself, as well as guidelines for styling and visibility of primary/orientation streets and labels.
All Site icons and site labels should disappear when the player zooms out to a zoom level below 12.5.
Reduce the `inset` property on the glyphs to 10%.
Can we extend the white coloring of the primary and orientation streets as far into the blur as those streets are defined?

Could you add a 'joke' point on the map at the location of my real-world address?  I live at 38 Caribou Trail in Wasaga Beach, Ontario.  A little blue dot with "I Live Here!" as the tooltip would be perfect.

The hover-over effect for districts should change as follows:

1. Remove the fill effect for hover-over
2. Add a thin dotted red border around the district (being mindful of the 'no district borders at map edges' rule)
3. Smoothly scale up the size, opacity, and brightness of the district name, and tween its color to bright red.
Instead of filling in the entire area of regions, can we apply an "inner glow" effect and reduce the weight of the stroke so it's a little subtler?
Is it possible to have the pulsing border of a selected district appear painted over the white orientation roads, but _under_ the labels for those roads?
When a site is selected in the site menu, the map should pan to that site as with Districts, and the District containing that site should be selected.

Is it possible to interface the player map with the Storyteller Dashboard live, during play, so that player pins can appear on the player map in the same way they appear on the current in-game map hud?  (Please reply in chat once you've finished resolving the rest of the pins.)

At desktop resolutions, the district information panel should be fully replaced with the corresponding district image in `public/assets/images/districtHeaders`, centered horizontally at the top of the screen.  (No deselect "X" button is necessary; clicking the District on the map is enough to deselect.)

Hovering over this top display bar should pop up a small version of the District card (located in `public/assets/images/districtCards`) as a tooltip. Clicking on the district header should bring up a modal displaying the District card full-size, with the map darkened beneath the modal. Clicking off of the modal should close it (but should NOT cause an interaction with the map at the asme time -- i.e. clicking off of the modal to close it should not also select the district that happens to be beneath the click).

Simultaneously, the corresponding district domain control bonus image should be displayed centered at the bottom of the screen (found in `public/assets/images/districtFooters`)

For mobile resolutions, the current format should remain.

Add buttons on the side for the "Coteries", "Hunting" and "Homestead" menus, using the corresponding glyphs in `public/assets/icons/left_panel`. Details on how to implement these menus, as well as the Domains menu, can be found in `dev/Left Sidebar Menus.md`.
The animated expanding menus on the left sidebar need to expand out a bit farther to the right, so that when they expand downwards, they don't overlap the other buttons on the left sidebar.
Remove the +/- zoom buttons: Desktop users can scroll wheel, mobile users can pinch zoom.

Hovering over a site icon should popup a small image of either their site card (in `public/assets/images/siteCards`) or, in the case of the six mapped site hub locations, their site hub card (in `public/assets/images/siteHubCards`).  Clicking on a site should bring up a full-screen view of the site card _and_ the District card (located in `public/assets/images/districtCards`), with the District Card on top and the Site Card on the bottom, with the map darkened behind the modal overlay.  Clicking off of either card should close the overlay. 

Because site hub cards are quite large, instead of displaying both, display the site hub card first, with a note to "click to view District" beneath it; clicking on the site hub card will switch over to displaying (just) the district card, and vice versa, until the user clicks off of the modal.

Please use the new "Show On Map" column in the EXPORT_LOCATION_SITES data set to determine which sites should be shown on the map; hide all sites that have map locations but where this value is FALSE.
